01

Why I volunteer

Belonging begins with how we show up for one another.

Starting again in a new city has made me understand how much belonging matters.

I want to volunteer not only to give my time, but to offer the kind of presence that helps someone feel welcomed, respected, and a little less alone. I’m especially drawn to community wellbeing, outreach, newcomer inclusion, and opportunities to connect with young adults, seniors, and the wider public.

“Meaningful support often starts with something simple: noticing, listening, and staying long enough to understand.”

At Anfu Elder Care Home, I helped older adults with everyday, non-clinical needs — mobility, meals, laundry, and accompanied walking. The work was quiet and practical. It reminded me that care is often expressed through patience, steadiness, and a willingness to help with what is actually needed.

02

How I show up

Four ways I try to be useful.

01

Listen before acting

I try to understand what a person is experiencing before offering advice or deciding what help should look like.

02

Make room for others

I notice who has not been heard and create a safer opening for quieter voices to enter the conversation.

03

Keep a group connected

Whether hosting, facilitating, or working behind the scenes, I help people feel comfortable enough to participate.

04

Follow through

I value dependable, practical contribution — including the work that is ordinary, unseen, or simply needs to be done.

03

Training, mentoring & confidence

Confidence grows when people feel safe enough to try.

My most meaningful work has rarely been about delivering information. It has been about lowering the barrier to participation.

At Proudly, I introduced practical AI applications to more than 100 employees. Some were curious; others worried that AI might replace them. I listened to those concerns and framed the sessions around everyday support, human judgement, and small first successes.

At Xinhe, I mentored more than 100 university students across a multi-year internship partnership. I learned to look beyond the most confident voices. When I noticed one quiet student’s thoughtful notes and creative ideas, I invited her into the discussion without putting her on the spot. Her idea was adopted, and her team went on to place first in its assessment.

04

Hosting, livestreaming & communication

Helping a room feel like a community.

Years of hosting, livestreaming, and group facilitation taught me that communication is not about holding the spotlight. It is about reading the room, helping people feel at ease, and keeping everyone connected when the unexpected happens.

A moment I remember

When the sound system failed during a university event, I stepped into the audience and began an impromptu conversation while the technical team recovered. What could have felt like an awkward gap became a shared moment. That experience still shapes how I respond to uncertainty: stay calm, pay attention, and help the group move forward together.

05

Strength for the long road

Endurance has shaped how I keep a commitment.

Long-distance running and high-altitude trekking have taught me to prepare carefully, pace myself, accept discomfort, and keep moving without losing awareness of the people around me.

What I hope to contribute

A dependable pair of hands — and a welcoming presence.

I’m currently looking for flexible volunteer opportunities in Vancouver where I can meet people, support meaningful programmes, and keep learning how to serve this community well.

  • Community wellbeing and public outreach
  • Newcomer inclusion and community connection
  • Young-adult programmes and group facilitation
  • Seniors’ companionship and non-clinical support
  • Events, multilingual engagement, and programme support

I try to arrive without assuming I already know what someone needs: listen first, respect their choices, and offer support without taking over.

Let’s connect

If you’re building a kinder, more connected community, I’d be glad to help.
